# `Q-2-55` — Class Specifier Before Identifier in Attribute

> Inside `{...}` attribute braces, an identifier (`#id`) appears after a class specifier (`.name`).

## What this means

The attribute specifier syntax requires the identifier (`#id`) to come first. This error fires when an identifier appears after a class specifier.

The parser reports the error at the out-of-place token and adds a hint
that rewrites your own attribute list in the accepted order, using the
identifiers, classes and values you actually wrote.

Quarto 2 is deliberately stricter here than Pandoc's reader, which accepts
these in any order. The fixed order keeps documents consistent: identity,
classes, then configuration.

## How to fix

Put the identifier first, then the classes, then the key-value pairs:

```markdown
[foo]{#id .class}    <!-- correct -->
[foo]{.class #id}    <!-- triggers Q-2-55 -->
```

This applies to every construct that takes an attribute list: spans,
images, inline code, editorial marks (`[++ ]`, `[-- ]`, `[>> ]`, `[!! ]`),
headings, fenced divs, editorial divs and fenced code blocks.

`qmd-syntax-helper convert -r attribute-ordering -i <file>` rewrites
attribute lists into the accepted order for you.

## Example

The parser flags this input:

```markdown
[foo]{.class #id}
```
